title: France manufacturing turnover falls 0.7% in June 2026
summary:
France's manufacturing turnover fell 0.7 per cent in June 2026, after a 1.7 per cent drop in the previous reading, INSEE said.
Seasonally and working-day adjusted data point to weaker European production-linked turnover for textile and apparel sourcing teams.
As turnover indices reflect price and activity, INSEE advised using producer price and industrial production indices to separate the two.

title: Higher LNG prices, supply shortages compound Bangladesh gas crisis
summary:
The deepening gas and electricity crises in Bangladesh have been compounded by a sharp rise in global LNG prices and supply shortages coinciding with high power demand. 
Industrial production has been severely hit, with 70 per cent of the production capacity of gas-dependent factories staying unutilised, pressuring the export sector. 
The energy crunch is no longer confined to power-intensive industries.

title: Can Bangladesh’s fiscal reset put growth on a faster track?
summary:
Bangladesh is set to shift its fiscal year from July-June to April-March, with FY2027-28 a nine-month transition before April 2028. 
A five-member committee will identify constitutional, legal and financial-system changes needed to implement the calendar. 
An April start could create a three-month dry-season window for faster construction, but experts warn old bottlenecks may persist.

title: US GDP growth slows to 1.5% in Q2 2026
summary:
US real GDP rose at a 1.5 per cent annual rate in Q2 2026, slower than 2.1 per cent in Q1.
Consumer spending, exports and investment supported growth, while government spending fell and imports increased.
For apparel and textile sourcing teams, higher imports and firmer demand signals come alongside elevated purchase and PCE price gains.
BEA annual updates start September 30, 2026.

title: Uzbekistan & China deepen textile ties to expand global reach
summary:
Uzbekistan and China are deepening textile co-operation through investment, technology transfer, joint manufacturing and market access. 
Chinese companies are exploring production and manufacturing orders in Uzbekistan, while Fergana is seeking stronger business ties with China. 
Uzbekistan exported $2.6 billion in textiles in 2025 and targets $4 billion in textile exports in 2026.

title: EU goods trade rises in Q2 2026 as China, US lead
summary:
EU goods imports from non-EU countries reached €701.8 billion (~$816 billion) in Q2 2026, while exports totalled €680.0 billion (~$791 billion).
Imports rose 9.9 per cent and exports 5.4 per cent from Q1, signalling firmer cross-border goods flows.
China led suppliers and the US led export destinations, key for sourcing and sales teams tracking partner shifts.

title: Women-led Vietnamese firms urged to strengthen sustainable exports
summary:
Vietnam has urged women-owned and gender-responsive enterprises to strengthen traceability, transparency and sustainable practices as global markets tighten supply-chain requirements. 
Officials said tariff preferences under FTAs are no longer sufficient, with exporters required to meet standards covering sustainability, labour, environmental compliance, product safety and corporate responsibility.

title: India's 36% Cambodia trade surge sets up a new textile opportunity
summary:
India-Cambodia trade rose more than 36 per cent to $406.78 million in 2025-26, while April-June 2026 trade increased 63.25 per cent YoY.
Cambodia is India's eighth-largest ASEAN partner and accounts for just 0.31 per cent of India-ASEAN trade.
Both countries face a 10 per cent US forced-labour duty, weakening the case for shifting apparel production to Cambodia.

title: Nylon staple fibre lags chip rally, signals further price catch-up
summary:
Nylon staple fibre in China rose 4.32 per cent to $2.172/kg by August 26, lagging nylon 6 chips and caprolactam.
Producers first absorbed feedstock gains via inventory, contracts and margin compression, then repriced fibre faster after August 20.
Mills, fabric makers and sourcing teams face likely further fibre catch-up as chip tightness and autumn-winter demand lift costs.

title: North India cotton yarn notices mixed trend, overseas demand better
summary:
Ludhiana cotton yarn prices rose by ₹2 per kg on strong export orders, while Delhi stayed stable amid weak domestic buying.
Higher yarn costs squeezed weaving margins as fabric and garment buyers resisted price increases.
Panipat recycled yarn held steady ahead of expected festive demand, while North India cotton prices steadied after Wednesday’s surge.

title: Cambodia’s ASEAN apparel exports rise but trail Asia-Pacific growth
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports to ASEAN rose 5.5 per cent to $157.242 million in H1 2026.
Growth outpaced the 2.1 per cent rise in worldwide apparel exports but trailed Asia-Pacific’s 6.8 per cent expansion.
ASEAN held 10.4 per cent of Cambodia’s Asia-Pacific apparel exports and nearly 1.7 per cent of worldwide shipments.
T-shirts, jerseys and coats grew; trousers, shorts and shirts declined.

title: Kontoor Brands appoints C.J. King to lead Helly Hansen North America
summary:
Kontoor Brands has appointed C.J. King as general manager, Helly Hansen, North America, Sport, effective August 31. 
King will lead Helly Hansen's North America Sport business, spanning commercial strategy and marketplace execution. 
His Arc'teryx, Smartwool, PEARL iZUMi and The North Face experience signals focus on technical outdoor apparel channels and US growth.

title: China's 19% Japan apparel decline could open India a $31bn market
summary:
India ships garments to Japan duty-free since 2011, but still accounts for under 2 per cent of the market.
Japan’s apparel imports from China fell for four straight years to $11.23 billion in 2024, over 19 per cent below 2021.
China’s share falls below half in 2025 as Vietnam and Bangladesh gain from China-plus-one sourcing by buyers and manufacturers.

title: US' Somnigroup announces new president of Leggett & Platt
summary:
Somnigroup International has appointed Tyson Hagale as President of Leggett & Platt, effective immediately, with oversight responsibility for the entire company.
Hagale, a 25-year veteran of Leggett & Platt and former Bedding Products segment president, will report to CEO Karl Glassman.
Hagale is recognised for his leadership in restructuring and industry expertise.

title: US' Somnigroup completes $2.3 bn Leggett & Platt combination
summary:
Somnigroup has completed its all-stock combination with Leggett & Platt, valued at $2.3 billion including debt. 
The merged bedding and engineered components group operates over 170 plants in 37 countries, backed by more than 36,000 staff. 
The deal deepens Somnigroup’s vertical integration, secures a critical supply-chain element and lifts annual run-rate synergy expectations to $75 million.

title: Skechers is now the second-largest footwear brand in US
summary:
Skechers is now the second-largest footwear brand by units sold in the US, driven by affordable comfort, work, kids’ and performance styles. 
The gain raises competition across US casual, fashion and sport footwear ranges, supported by comfort technologies and athlete-led visibility. 
The brand sells through 700-plus US stores, its web shop and retail partners, relevant to footwear sourcing teams.

title: Belgium's Van de Velde posts H1 revenue growth on D2C strength
summary:

Reported revenue rose 5.2 per cent to €115.7 million (~$135.02 million), while net profit increased to €16.1 million (~$18.79 million). 
D2C revenue surged 15.2 per cent to €34.2 million (~$39.91 million), supported by product innovation and digital expansion.

title: New Zealand apparel imports up in July, but cumulative down
summary:

January–July imports fell 1.6 per cent to NZ$1.197 billion; knitted apparel declined 1 per cent and non-knitted 2.4 per cent.
Apparel exports fell 19.3 per cent in July but rose 1.1 per cent in January–July; knitted fabric imports rose 21.6 per cent cumulatively.

title: US apparel sourcing could shift to fewer, bigger strategic vendors
summary:
US fashion companies sourced apparel from 49 countries in 2026, up from 46 in 2025, but only 21.1 per cent expect to add countries.
TexPro says US HS 61 and 62 apparel imports fell 7.77 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026.
